title: Briefing for 2026-10-05
intro: Good morning. Here is your briefing for 2026-10-05: US markets, global news, and the Philippines, in five minutes.
us: Men are losing ground in the labor market. Here's why. Labor market faltered in September as jobs increased by just 29,000, unemployment rate rose to 4.2%. The September jobs report will be released Friday. Here's what to expect. Fed’s preferred gauge showed core inflation at 3.0% in August, much lighter than expected. The Fed's main inflation measure will be released Wednesday. Here's what to expect. America's Canadian import restrictions come into force. Here are the products barred from entry.
global: Yemen's government announces all-out war to reclaim land from Houthis. Polls close in Brazil as Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro remain neck and neck. Christa Pike's prognosis still unclear after failed execution, lawyer says. Indian police accused of sexually harassing journalists at protest. G7 to release millions of barrels of oil and diesel after Trump threat. Suppliers pile pressure on government over energy bills.
philippines: For advocates, CHED’s openness to lived names policy brings hope. ‘Forgotten Island’: Filipino American stories are Filipino stories. Carlos Yulo to get P4 million for golden double as medalists cash in on Asian Games success. Meet Jaime Tan Cruz, business partner of the Duterte family.
outro: That's your briefing. Have a great day.
